| Feature | Description |
|---|---|

| **Gas vs. Imported LNG** |  |

| - *Phu My 5.3, Nhon Trach 5, etc.* | Fed by **imported LNG** (via terminals like Thi Vai, Son My, Hai Phong) |
| **O Mon 3** | Hybrid—starts with **local gas**, later switch to **imported LNG** (via planned Kien Giang/Soc Trang terminals) |
| **Soc Trang LNG-to-power** | Also called **Ca Mau 3** — 3,000 MW LNG plant, fed from **Soc Trang LNG Terminal** |

- **Capacity for Ca Mau 3** and **Soc Trang LNG-to-power** is combined in some reports; treated as **3,000 MW total**.

- **Lach Huyen LNG Terminal** (Hai Phong) is a **new project**, but Lach Huyen LNG-to-power is a separate 1,500 MW plant.

#### **1) LNG Import Terminals (Infrastructure Only)**
- These **do not include power capacity**—they enable LNG-to-power plants.
- Sources: **MoIT PDP8 Master Plan (2023)**, **EVN reports**, **PV Gas**.

#### **2) Gas & LNG-to-Power Plants**
| Plant | Status | Key Notes |
|------|--------|---------|
| **Son My Bac 1** | Operational (2025) | First LNG plant fed by **Son My terminal** |
| **O Mon 3** | U/C (2026) | Starts with **local gas**, **switches to imported LNG** via Kien Giang terminal |
| **Nhon Trach 5** | Planned (PDP8) | Adding **850 MW LNG unit** to existing gas fleet |
| **Hai Phong LNG-to-power (2,000 MW)** | Planned (PDP8) | Largest single LNG plant, fed via **Hai Phong terminal** |
| **Soc Trang (Ca Mau 3)** | Planned (PDP8) | 3,000 MW; largest LNG plant in Vietnam |

- **Duyen Hai 2** (1,120 MW) → **Suspended** due to financing and environmental concerns.
- **Duyen Hai 3 Extension** (1,300 MW) → Planned **second expansion**.
